ex.en: The company held a luncheon for retiring staff.
ex.zh: 公司為退休員工舉辦了午宴。

ex.en: We are invited to a business luncheon on Monday.
ex.zh: 我們受邀參加星期一的商務午餐會。

luncheon.en: a formal meal in the middle of the day

ex.en: Let's meet at lunchtime.
ex.zh: 我們午餐時間見吧。

ex.en: The restaurant is always busy at lunchtime.
ex.zh: 這家餐廳午餐時間總是很忙。

lunchtime.en: the time of day when people usually eat their midday meal

ex.en: She left a lucrative job to start her own business.
ex.zh: 她辭去高薪工作，自己創業。

ex.en: The company won a lucrative contract.
ex.zh: 這家公司拿下了一份利潤豐厚的合約。

ex.en: That boy threw a lump of rock.
ex.zh: 那個男孩丟了一塊石頭。

ex.en: I bumped my head against the door and got a lump.
ex.zh: 我的頭撞到門，腫了一個包。

ex.en: Do you take one lump of sugar or two?
ex.zh: 你要加一顆方糖還是兩顆？

lump.en: a small solid piece of something with no particular shape, or a swelling under the skin

lump.zh: lump sum：一次付清的款項、一筆總額

ex.en: You can pay the fee in a lump sum.
ex.zh: 這筆費用可以一次付清。

ex.en: She received a lump sum when she retired.
ex.zh: 她退休時領了一筆一次性的退休金。

lump.en: a single payment of money given all at once, not in parts

ex.en: The store lured customers with big discounts.
ex.zh: 這家店用大折扣吸引顧客。

ex.en: They tried to lure him to a rival company.
ex.zh: 他們想把他挖角到競爭對手的公司。

lure.en: to attract someone or something by offering something nice

ex.en: The lure of a higher salary was hard to resist.
ex.zh: 更高薪水的誘惑讓人難以抗拒。

ex.en: Many young people come for the lure of city life.
ex.zh: 許多年輕人是被城市生活的吸引力而來的。

ex.en: Will you have time to have lunch with me?
ex.zh: 你有空跟我吃午餐嗎？

ex.en: If we begin early, we can finish by lunch.
ex.zh: 如果我們早點開始，就能在午餐前完成。

ex.en: The students' lunch period is from twelve to one.
ex.zh: 學生的午餐時間是十二點到一點。

lunch.en: the meal that you eat in the middle of the day

ex.en: It was lucky for you that you found it.
ex.zh: 你能找到它真是幸運。

ex.en: This year has been a lucky one for him.
ex.zh: 今年對他來說是幸運的一年。

ex.en: Allan was lucky and passed the tax accountant examination.
ex.zh: 艾倫很幸運地考過了稅務師考試。

lucky.en: having good things happen to you by chance

ex.en: Seven is my lucky number.
ex.zh: 七是我的幸運數字。

ex.en: He always wears his lucky shirt to interviews.
ex.zh: 他每次面試都穿他的幸運襯衫。

lucky.en: believed to bring good things to you

ex.en: Sooner or later, his luck will run out.
ex.zh: 他的好運遲早會用完。

ex.en: I don't believe that black cats cause bad luck.
ex.zh: 我不相信黑貓會帶來厄運。

ex.en: A little bit of luck sometimes leads to an unexpected success.
ex.zh: 一點點運氣有時會帶來意想不到的成功。

luck.en: good or bad things that happen to you by chance

luck.zh: good luck / best of luck：祝好運、祝順利

ex.en: We wish you the best of luck in your endeavors.
ex.zh: 祝您一切順利。

ex.en: Good luck with your job interview!
ex.zh: 祝你面試順利！

luck.en: said to wish someone success in something they are going to do

ex.en: Advertisements urge us to buy luxuries.
ex.zh: 廣告慫恿我們買奢侈品。

ex.en: Travelling is a luxury I can't afford.
ex.zh: 旅行對我來說是負擔不起的奢侈。

ex.en: In the United States the automobile is a necessity and not a luxury.
ex.zh: 在美國，汽車是必需品而不是奢侈品。

luxury.en: something expensive that you enjoy but do not really need

ex.en: On the seventh floor, you can find four luxury restaurants.
ex.zh: 七樓有四間豪華餐廳。

ex.en: We stayed at a luxury hotel in Bangkok.
ex.zh: 我們在曼谷住了一間豪華飯店。

luxury.en: very expensive and of the highest quality

ex.en: He is afraid of getting lung cancer.
ex.zh: 他很怕得肺癌。

ex.en: Smokers are far more likely to develop lung cancer than non-smokers are.
ex.zh: 吸菸者罹患肺癌的機率遠高於不吸菸者。

ex.en: Regular exercise helps keep your lungs healthy.
ex.zh: 規律運動有助於維持肺部健康。

lung.en: one of the two organs in your chest that you use to breathe

lung.zh: at the top of one's lungs：扯開嗓門、放聲

ex.en: He shouted at the top of his lungs.
ex.zh: 他扯開嗓門大喊。

ex.en: The kids sang at the top of their lungs.
ex.zh: 孩子們放聲高歌。

ex.en: The new theatre looks very luxurious.
ex.zh: 新劇院看起來非常豪華。

ex.en: We stayed in a luxurious hotel near the beach.
ex.zh: 我們住在海邊一家豪華飯店。

ex.en: The office has a luxurious lobby.
ex.zh: 這棟辦公大樓有個豪華的大廳。

ex.en: The luminous numbers on the clock glowed in the dark.
ex.zh: 時鐘上的夜光數字在黑暗中發亮。

ex.en: She had luminous eyes that seemed to shine.
ex.zh: 她有一雙明亮的眼睛，彷彿會發光。

luminous.en: giving out light, especially in the dark

ex.en: We loaded a lot of luggage into the car.
ex.zh: 我們往車裡裝了很多行李。

ex.en: I don't like traveling with lots of luggage.
ex.zh: 我出門不喜歡帶很多行李。

ex.en: Let me help you with your luggage.
ex.zh: 讓我幫您提行李。

luggage.en: the bags and cases that you take with you when you travel

ex.en: Luke is a short and popular name for boys.
ex.zh: 盧克是個簡短又受歡迎的男孩名字。

ex.en: Luke is one of the four Gospels in the New Testament.
ex.zh: 路加福音是新約聖經四部福音書之一。

ex.en: Lucy drew a beautiful picture for her grandmother.
ex.zh: 露西畫了一幅漂亮的畫送給她的奶奶。

ex.en: Lucy forgot her umbrella on the train again.
ex.zh: 露西又把雨傘忘在火車上了。

ex.en: The hills were lush and green after the rain.
ex.zh: 雨後山丘一片蒼翠。

ex.en: They walked through a lush garden full of flowers.
ex.zh: 他們穿過一座花團錦簇、綠意盎然的花園。

ex.en: The lunar surface is covered with craters and dust.
ex.zh: 月球表面佈滿隕石坑和塵土。

ex.en: A lunar eclipse will be visible tonight if the sky is clear.
ex.zh: 如果天空晴朗，今晚可以看到月蝕。

ex.en: Families gather for dinner on the eve of the Lunar New Year.
ex.zh: 農曆新年前夕，家人會聚在一起吃團圓飯。

ex.en: The festival follows the lunar calendar, so the date changes each year.
ex.zh: 這個節日依照農曆，所以日期每年都不同。

ex.en: Luckily, we arrived at the station just before the train left.
ex.zh: 幸虧我們在火車開走前剛好趕到車站。

ex.en: I dropped my phone, but luckily the screen did not break.
ex.zh: 我的手機掉了，但幸好螢幕沒破。

ex.en: A cat lurked in the bushes, waiting for a bird.
ex.zh: 一隻貓潛伏在灌木叢中等著鳥。

ex.en: Danger can lurk in unexpected places.
ex.zh: 危險可能潛伏在意想不到的地方。

ex.en: The workers loaded lumber onto the truck for the new house.
ex.zh: 工人們把蓋新房子用的木材裝上卡車。

ex.en: The price of lumber has risen sharply this year.
ex.zh: 今年木材的價格大幅上漲。

ex.en: The old bus lumbered slowly up the hill.
ex.zh: 那輛老舊的公車笨重地慢慢爬上山坡。

ex.en: A bear lumbered out of the forest toward the river.
ex.zh: 一頭熊笨拙地走出森林，朝河邊走去。

ex.en: Luxembourg is a small country in Western Europe.
ex.zh: 盧森堡是西歐的一個小國。

ex.en: Luxembourg is bordered by Belgium, France and Germany.
ex.zh: 盧森堡與比利時、法國和德國接壤。

ex.en: They attend a Lutheran church near their home.
ex.zh: 他們去家附近的一間路德教會做禮拜。

ex.en: The Lutheran school was founded over a century ago.
ex.zh: 那所路德教會學校創立已超過一百年。

ex.en: My neighbor is a Lutheran and goes to church every Sunday.
ex.zh: 我的鄰居是路德教會的教友，每週日都上教堂。

ex.en: Many Lutherans live in northern Europe.
ex.zh: 許多路德教會教友住在北歐。

ex.en: The bus lurched forward and everyone grabbed a handrail.
ex.zh: 公車猛然往前一晃，大家都抓住扶手。

ex.en: He lurched down the hallway after the long party.
ex.zh: 長長的派對後，他在走廊上搖搖晃晃地走著。

ex.en: The boat gave a sudden lurch to the left.
ex.zh: 船突然往左猛晃了一下。

ex.en: I felt a lurch in my stomach when the elevator dropped.
ex.zh: 電梯下墜時，我的胃一陣翻攪。

ex.en: It is ludicrous to pay that much for a plain T-shirt.
ex.zh: 一件普通 T 恤要花那麼多錢，真是荒唐。

ex.en: The idea sounded ludicrous at first, but it worked.
ex.zh: 這個點子乍聽之下很荒謬，但卻行得通。

ex.en: The cat lunged at the toy mouse.
ex.zh: 那隻貓猛撲向玩具老鼠。

ex.en: He lunged for the ball but missed it.
ex.zh: 他撲向球，卻沒碰到。

ex.en: The fencer made a quick lunge at his opponent.
ex.zh: 擊劍選手朝對手快速刺出一劍。

ex.en: With a sudden lunge, the dog grabbed the stick.
ex.zh: 那隻狗突然一撲，叼住了樹枝。
